intro_en: The Israel National Trail runs along the southern Carmel as far as "the Nose" (Hotem HaCarmel) – the southern tip of the Carmel – from which it glides down to the plain of the Carmel Coast.
character_en: (For those walking from north to south) Walking in gentle terrain, with no hard ascents or descents apart from a slightly steep descent at the end. Alternating between dirt roads and hiking trails. The route is partly shaded, with shade spots available along the way.
shortcuts_en: The route is modular and can be walked in short sections.
transport_en: Oren Junction on Road 4. Kerem Maharal or Ofer Junction on Road 4. The turn-off from Road 4 to Beit Hanania.
pois_en: Gan Yaron; the winery, the Aaronsohn House museum, Binyamin Pool and the historic cemetery in Zichron Yaakov; Ramat HaNadiv and the gardens around the burial estate of Baron Rothschild; the antiquities and lookout of Horvat Aqav; the Moran Lookout; the Binyamina quarries.
description_en:
We set out from the entrance road to Moshav Kerem Maharal, on a dirt road that heads south towards the KKL-JNF offices compound. We pass the offices and continue south along the road. We advance until the trail turns right into the stream channel and into the woodland. This is a short stretch on a shaded, pretty hiking trail.
On leaving the woodland, the trail returns to a dirt road that leads to the entrance road to Moshav Ofer. After crossing the road, we return to a hiking trail through the woodland for a short distance and then go back to walking on a dirt road.
The Israel National Trail continues south on a dirt road, alongside a high-voltage power line with tall pylons. When we reach the foot of Givat Talimon, the trail leaves the dirt road, climbs the hill and crosses it. We can take in Horvat Talimon, although there are not many visible remains on the ground, and look down from above at the surroundings we are hiking through.
We descend the southern side of the hill to a white dirt road – the access road to the nearby quarries. Take care and watch out for truck traffic.
We leave the main road and turn right onto a dirt road that runs along the edge of a cultivated valley with fields and vineyards. We walk until we meet the entrance road to the Meir Shfeya youth village, with the houses of the northern neighbourhoods of Zichron Yaakov visible to the south.
The trail continues along the shoulder of the entrance road to Meir Shfeya, crosses Shfeya Junction and continues south on a pavement beside the road. A short distance before the next junction, the trail crosses the road eastwards – onto a paved road.
We walk along the road between the farmland and the highway as far as the road bridge, turn right and pass under the bridge. On the other side of the bridge, we continue on a dirt road eastwards, towards the tall pylons visible ahead. When the road passes under the high-voltage line, we turn right onto a dirt road and advance about 2 km southwards, beneath the power line. We reach a junction with a blue-marked dirt road and turn with it westwards, towards Zichron Yaakov.
A short distance before the trail enters the streets of the moshava, we can spot on the right a sign for "Gan Yaron" – a shaded corner in the woodland with stone benches and a water point, suitable for a break and a rest. The garden was established in memory of Yaron Amitai, a reservist killed in the Second Lebanon War.
We enter Zichron Yaakov with the trail, onto Ma'of HaTzipor Street. We reach a T-junction and turn right, towards the historic winery, Carmel Winery, founded at the end of the 19th century at the initiative of Baron Rothschild.
From the winery we continue to the historic street of the moshava – HaMeyasdim (Founders) Street – which today is a touristic pedestrian mall. Along the street we pass important sites connected to the history of the moshava: the synagogue, Binyamin Pool, the Aaronsohn House and the houses of the first settlers.
The trail leaves the historic street through the Yishai Gate towards the historic cemetery. Carved on the stone wall at the front of the cemetery are sayings of the founders of the moshava.
Via HaShita Street, the trail reaches a pedestrian entrance to Ramat HaNadiv. After a short walk on woodland tracks, we reach the gardens and the tomb compound of the philanthropist Baron Rothschild, who, among other things, founded Zichron Yaakov as well as other moshavot around the country.
The marked trail skirts the gardens, reaches the car park and continues south from there, but it is recommended to turn right and pass through the well-tended gardens, which are open to visitors on weekdays between 8:00 and 16:00.
South of the car park, the Israel National Trail continues along a red-marked trail to the edge of Ramat HaNadiv and to an archaeological site – Horvat Aqav (Khirbet al-Aqab). It is worth touring the site and also looking west over the Carmel coastal plain – from Atlit to Hadera.
The trail turns south, making its way along the edge of the plateau to "Hotem HaCarmel" (the Nose of the Carmel) – the southern tip of the Carmel. The trail descends via the Moran Lookout – named after Moran Vardi, a naval commando officer killed in battle in Nablus in 2004.
From the lookout we can enjoy a fine view: to the west, the coastal plain – from Nahal Taninim, through the village of Jisr az-Zarqa, to the chimneys of the Hadera power station; to the south, the moshava of Binyamina and, east of it, the Nadiv Valley.
We descend from the lookout on a road that runs along the edge of the rehabilitated Binyamina quarry. At the bottom of the descent we pass several historic installations that were left in place to tell the story of the old quarry, which began operating as early as the 1930s.
Further on, the trail turns sharply west, advances parallel to the channel of Nahal Taninim for a short distance and reaches a safe passage beneath the railway line at the Nahal Taninim bridge.
Please note: the trail passes beneath the Haifa – Tel Aviv railway line, which carries heavy train traffic. Crossing the tracks over the bridge is dangerous. For your safety, cross the line only underneath the bridge. In winter it may be necessary to pass under the tracks through shallow water.
After passing the railway, we walk west alongside Nahal Taninim. An avenue of cypresses marks the point where we turn left towards Beit Hanania and a bridge that allows passage beneath Road 4. In the underpass beneath the road we pass the remains of an ancient aqueduct – part of the water system of Caesarea. The ancient aqueducts will accompany the trail as far as Caesarea. From here it is a short way to the end point on the entrance road to Moshav Beit Hanania.
author_en: Omer Shapira, Content Coordinator, Tourism Department, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel (SPNI).
